transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-04-06 15:30 UTC | Duration ~52m
Attendees: Jesse Carter, Maya Singh (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Priya Narang, Diego Morales (HelixHealth)

--- Summary ---
(automated) Weekly sync for POC onboarding progress, infra access, and latency bench follow-up.

--- Topics ---
- Staging credentials and ephemeral keys
- Gateway/auth integration + terraform snippets
- Tail latency observed in nightly runs
- KV cache warmup strategy and batch sizes
- Security: KMS/HSM mapping, SSO/SAML, audit logs
- Next steps and owners

00:00:08 Jesse: ok good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. quick check-in, we've got 50 minutes, want to cover creds, the tail-latency that diego flagged, and next steps for staging.
00:00:18 Liam: Yeah thanks Jesse. Quick note, Priya had to hop from another call, but we're all here.
00:00:25 Priya: hi everyone, I might jump in with security questions, thanks.
00:00:30 Maya: Hey - Maya from Redwood, I'll be owning the gateway and runbook docs, so I'll share the snippets afterwards.
00:00:36 Jesse: sweet. Diego, do you want to summarize the latency find? I saw your note in the sheet but want to hear context.
00:00:43 Diego: sure. so last night's run, we did 10k requests over a 1 hour window against the hosted endpoint, we saw avg p95 ~180ms but p99 spikes to 2.4s intermittently. it seemed correlated with cold KV cache hits and bursts of long sequences.
00:01:02 Jesse: hmm okay. when you say KV cache you mean Redwood's prefix cache, right?
00:01:07 Diego: yeah, or specifically the K V cache—there's an initial miss pattern when many parallel sessions start. we warmed a few times but maybe not enough. also noticed a slight throughput drop when we hit token limit and fallback quantized path kicked in.
00:01:24 Maya: quick clarification — the runtime will route to a quantized variant when memory pressure crosses threshold, so that can add latency jitter; also kernel selection sometimes adds small pauses.
00:01:36 Priya: from security, before we dive deep - we need to see how keys rotate. KMS integration, HSM binding, and how long tokens/ephemeral creds live in staging. also audit logging retention.
00:01:50 Jesse: fair. Maya, can you go through the credential flow we recommend for staging?
00:01:55 Maya: yep. recommended flow: short-lived tokens via our gateway, ephemeral service account creds minted by the connector. rotate every 15 minutes for staging, 1 hour for lower-sensitivity dev. we provide terraform snippets to create the role and the connector config.
00:02:12 Liam: are those snippets generic? our infra team uses a custom bastion and private endpoints in our VPC, we need examples for VPC peering and transit gateway.
00:02:22 Maya: they include VPC endpoint examples and a simple route table change. I'll paste the snippet to the drive. it's not full prod ready but a good starting point.
00:02:33 Priya: also, SSO mapping — we need RBAC ties back to our SAML groups. can we map Redwood roles to our groups?
00:02:41 Jesse: yes we do S A M L SSO and group mapping; we can share the mapping pattern.
00:02:46 Diego: returning to latency - one thing I noticed was the generator model switching. when sequence length > 1k tokens in a single request the runtime sometimes moves to a different kernel path; do we have a knob to avoid variant switching?
00:02:59 Maya: there are policy knobs. you can pin to model-variant or set a memory-safety margin so it won't downshift to quantized paths until a hard threshold. downside is increased memory usage/cost.
00:03:12 Liam: tradeoff, yes. cost vs tail latency. we need more predictable p99 for user-facing flows.
00:03:18 Jesse: what's your p99 target for the pilot?
00:03:21 Liam: ideally <500ms for short prompts; <1.2s acceptable for longer subflows. but p99 >2s is too risky.
00:03:29 Jesse: okay good, actionable. Diego, can you run a benchmark with forced cache warmup, and one with the pin-to-variant policy?
00:03:36 Diego: yes I can. I'll run three sweep configs: cold-start, warm-KV, and pinned-variant. schedule at 6pm tonight.
00:03:44 Priya: on the logs piece - we need audit entries for model invocation, user id mapping, and request headers kept for 90 days. can you confirm what Redwood retains by default?
00:03:57 Maya: default is 30 days, and we can extend retention as an enterprise addon. we also stream audit logs to your customer-owned S3 or logging endpoint.
00:04:07 Priya: good. HSM — can we ensure encryption keys are in our HSM?
00:04:11 Jesse: yes — we support KMS integrations and in Private deployments can use customer HSM. for Hosted we can integrate to your cloud KMS for key wrapping.
00:04:21 Priya: ok please send the mapping doc.
00:04:25 Jesse: noted.
00:04:30 Speaker 1: (inaudible) sorry quick comment, are we planning to move to Dedicated for production?
00:04:35 Jesse: likely yes if throughput and SLOs demand it; we're covering both hosted and dedicated options in the pricing note.
00:04:42 Liam: timeline question — if pilot goes well by end of month can we be demo-ready for product folks first week of May?
00:04:50 Jesse: plausible. depends on access and KMS signoff.
00:04:55 Diego: one more bench note — tokenization differences changed payload size by about 6% between model versions, we should pin tokenizer too across runs.
00:05:05 Maya: good call. include tokenizer in the pinned config.
00:05:10 Jesse: ok let's talk failures — we saw one incident where gateway returned 503s during a secret rotation window.maya, can you explain typical rotation behavior?
00:05:18 Maya: rotation should be seamless with a double-write grace period on the connector; 503s occur if the connector container restarts and the gateway cache is cleared. suggestion: stagger rotations by node and use rolling restarts.
00:05:30 Diego: confirm — we saw 503s at 02:14 UTC when connector restarted. the logs show a short TTL miss on the gateway cache.
00:05:38 Priya: is there a way to schedule rotations outside our heavy traffic window?
00:05:42 Maya: yes you can set rotation window; we recommend off-peak. will include config in runbook.
00:05:48 Jesse: good. action items forming.
00:05:53 Liam: also curious about the quant profile — can we get a simple chart of accuracy delta vs cost when quantizing to 4-bit?
00:06:01 Maya: we have evaluation artifacts. we'll produce a small matrix: latency, cost per 1k tokens, and sample quality divergence for common prompts.
00:06:10 Diego: note that for our clinical summarization flow, quality drift over certain prompts is more visible. we'll supply a small prompt set to evaluate.
00:06:19 Priya: from security perspective, any model outputs persisted? we prefer ephemeral only unless explicitly stored.
00:06:24 Jesse: default is ephemeral for hosted, but you can configure retention. we'll default to no persistence for this pilot unless Helix requests it.
00:06:33 Speaker 2: (murmur)
00:06:40 Jesse: meta-question — what is the single blocker to hitting your May demo date? Liam?
00:06:45 Liam: SSO mapping and KMS signoff from security. plus stable p99 numbers.
00:06:51 Jesse: okay, so Priya is primary blocker owner. Priya, what do you need from us to do signoff?
00:06:57 Priya: I'd like the KMS mapping, retention SLA, and audit log delivery details. also a sample SOC2 evidence list and the roles mapping doc.
00:07:08 Jesse: we'll send those by EOD Friday.
00:07:12 Priya: and a lightweight diagram of the network flow for VPC peering.
00:07:17 Maya: I'll add that to the runbook.
00:07:20 Diego: quick tech detail - when you recommend warming KV cache, what's the typical warmup time?
00:07:26 Maya: depends on working set size; for 10k concurrent sessions, warmup can be 30-90 seconds, but continuous background refresh reduces misses.
00:07:35 Diego: ok we'll design a warmup script.
00:07:39 Jesse: let's outline the bench plan: Diego runs cold, warm, pinned-variant sweeps; Maya provides warmup script and runbook; Priya gets KMS and audit docs; Jesse sends pricing. schedule next sync next Tuesday?
00:07:53 Liam: works for us.
00:07:55 Jesse: great.
00:08:00 --- (jump forward in call after doc review / 32m later) ---
00:32:10 Jesse: picking back up - thanks for the questions earlier. I uploaded a quick spreadsheet showing pricing options: self-serve hosted, dedicated warm-pools, and private deployment. main diff is predictable throughput and lower p99 with dedicated.
00:32:24 Liam: I looked at that. for pilot we may try hosted with dedicated warm pools toggled, if cost allows.
00:32:31 Priya: want to confirm encryption at rest for logs; you said we can stream to our S3 — please ensure SSE-KMS is used.
00:32:39 Maya: yes we support SSE-KMS and can do envelope encryption with your key.
00:32:45 Diego: test result update — I ran a quick warmup test this morning, and p99 improved from 2.4s to 610ms when the cache was pre-populated; there are still a few outliers around 1.6s. attaching traces to the drive.
00:33:00 Jesse: that's encouraging. can you correlate the 1.6s outliers with the quant switch traces?
00:33:06 Diego: early look says yes, about 70% of those outliers coincide with a model-variant handoff.
00:33:12 Maya: one mitigation is to bump memory margin or reduce per-request max tokens to avoid falling into a different exec path.
00:33:20 Liam: reducing max tokens is not ideal for some user flows. is there a middle ground?
00:33:26 Maya: set a soft cap that triggers a warning rather than immediate switch; or choose a different model-variant with slightly higher memory but better latency profile.
00:33:36 Priya: question — if we pick dedicated nodes, do we still have to use the gateway or can we run direct VPC endpoints?
00:33:45 Jesse: you can run private deployments or dedicated in our region and use direct VPC endpoints; gateway is for hosted SaaS. we'll map options.
00:33:54 Liam: ok.
00:34:00 Diego: small nit - tokenizer pinning was easy, I added it to the run config. will include version hash in results.
00:34:07 Jesse: perfect.
00:34:12 Maya: for the warmup script, I'll include parallelized prefix writes and a staged ramp to avoid thundering herds.
00:34:20 Diego: good. that should help with the gateway cache TTL issue too.
00:34:26 Priya: regarding SOC2 evidence, do you have an example package we can review?
00:34:31 Jesse: yes, we have a SOC2 artifact pack and an SOC2 questionnaire; I'll share the redacted version.
00:34:38 Priya: and ISO?
00:34:40 Jesse: not in scope for this pilot but we can discuss.
00:34:44 Speaker 3: (crosstalk)
00:34:50 Jesse: ok wrapping up — let's do a quick recap and owners.
00:34:55 Jesse: Maya will share the runbook, gateway terraform snippets, runwarm script, and network diagram by 2027-04-09.
00:35:04 Maya: yes.
00:35:06 Jesse: Diego will run three benchmark sweeps tonight and post traces by 2027-04-07.
00:35:13 Diego: confirmed.
00:35:15 Jesse: Priya will provide KMS/HSM mapping requirements and SOC2 evidence list by 2027-04-13.
00:35:23 Priya: yes.
00:35:25 Jesse: Liam will coordinate infra team availability for the canary failover drill.
00:35:30 Liam: will set up a slot and send calendar invites.
00:35:33 Jesse: I will send updated pricing including dedicated warm-pool options by 2027-04-08 and schedule next sync for 2027-04-13.
00:35:42 Liam: thanks.
00:35:45 Priya: one last question, do we have a recommended SLO for cache hit rate?
00:35:50 Maya: aim for >=98% warm-hit for critical flows; we'll help with instrumentation.
00:35:57 Diego: okay we'll instrument.
00:36:00 Jesse: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
